text: dsh-rea 是 DeepSeek Harness 的逆向工程工具插件，通过官方 MCP 客户端桥接器启动上游 REA 服务，并将完整工具目录按需呈现给当前会话。用户可用 /rea 解锁工具、提交分析请求、查看状态或重新隐藏目录；插件还提供六种原版分析提示模板及动态补全，并在 Web 客户端菜单中预览和插入模板。它适合需要检查应用、二进制文件或运行行为的 DSH 用户。插件使用固定版本的 rea-agents 依赖和受支持的 Node.js 环境，可配置启动命令、工具超时及传给上游服务的环境变量。

dsh-rea connects DSH to REA reverse-engineering tools through MCP. Use /rea to reveal or hide the catalog per session, check its status, or forward an analysis request. The Web composer offers six prompts with argument forms and dynamic completions that users can preview and insert into a draft.
我想让 DSH 帮我分析一个 APK 或桌面程序。
需要在 DSH 里调用逆向分析工具检查二进制文件。
怎样按需打开一整套应用逆向工具，用完再隐藏？
想从聊天界面选择分析提示模板，并填写目标和参数。
能不能把逆向分析请求交给 MCP 工具处理？
I want DSH to inspect an APK with a full reverse-engineering tool catalog.
Let me reveal analysis tools only for the session that needs them.
I need prompt templates with live argument suggestions in the web composer.
按会话切换逆向工具目录：用户运行 /rea 显示完整上游工具，/rea off 隐藏，/rea status 查询当前状态；可将命令后面的请求继续发送给模型。
桥接上游 MCP 工具：启动固定版本的 REA stdio 服务，通过 DSH MCP 客户端注册上游工具，并由工具目录变化通知触发同步。
在 Web 的 / 菜单使用六种原版分析提示：浏览提示、填写参数、请求动态补全、预览原文并插入草稿。
按需注册原版分析 Skill：目录解锁时注册，最后一个会话重新隐藏后释放；也可将 exposure 设为 always。
dsh-rea 将 REA 作为本地 stdio 子进程连接，断线后不会自动重连；重启连接可能丢失当前目标及保留的证据状态，需显式重载插件。

dsh-rea README · dsh-rea：Full [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) 6.8.0 MCP tools and its original version-matched skill for DeepSeek Harness. English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Lazy by default:** the 229 tool schemas and the skill stay out of a request until you run `/rea` — 273,264 bytes per request saved in native mode (~171 KB in PTC) when they are not needed.
dsh-rea README · Lazy exposure (default since v0.4)：Tools and the skill are **per-agent lazily visible**; the protocol and the process do not change:

dsh-rea README · Lazy exposure (default since v0.4)：- The MCP connection, the single REA process, all six original prompts and completions are **always live** — the `/` menu works whether or not a session has revealed the catalog.
- Each agent starts with a `tools.restrict({ deny })` mask naming every current `mcp__rea__*` tool. Native schemas and the generated PTC SDK prompt are both projected from the same scope view, so both lose the catalog together.
- The skill is registered once at reveal time and released again when the last revealed session hides the catalog, so it costs nothing in sessions that never reveal — and stops costing anything after `/rea off`.
- A bridge re-sync (`notifications/tools/list_changed`) rebuilds every mask, so a new tool generation cannot slip through; agents that already revealed are never re-masked mid-task.
- A resumed session is judged from the `command/run` records already in its log: the records are replayed in order, so the last `/rea` or `/rea off` wins, `/rea status` records are ignored, and a session where you ran `/rea` yesterday is not hidden again today. An unreadable history means **hidden** — the catalogue is never revealed by accident.

dsh-rea README · `/rea` is the switch; keywords are not：```text
/rea                      reveal only, then wait for the request
/rea look at this apk      reveal, and forward that text to the model verbatim
/rea on                    same as a bare /rea
/rea status                report whether the catalog is hidden or revealed

The command reveals first, then queues everything after `/rea` as an **ordinary user message** — a resolved command never reaches the model, so not forwarding it would silently swallow your request.
section: `/rea` is the switch; keywords are not

text:
dsh-rea README · `/rea` is the switch; keywords are not：`/rea off` re-masks the tools immediately and is durable across a reload: a session that ends hidden stays hidden. It only affects the session that ran it.

**Why not infer from keywords:** inference is a guess, and a wrong guess costs the whole catalog (530 KB in native mode). It is also wrong precisely where it is most expensive — discussing this gate necessarily names its trigger words. `/rea` is the user saying it outright.

A keyword path still exists, opt-in:
section: `/rea` is the switch; keywords are not

dsh-rea README · `/rea` is the switch; keywords are not：```yaml
- id: dsh-rea
  config:
    keywordUnlock: true
```

Return to the previous always-on catalogue:

```yaml
- id: dsh-rea
  config:
    exposure: always
```

text:
dsh-rea README · What is preserved：- All **229 upstream tools**, including navigation, decompilation, Android/ADB, managed code, JavaScript/Electron and runtime analysis. No invented entry/navigate/analyze tiers.
- Original input schemas and descriptions, with stable DSH names `mcp__rea__<upstream-name>`.
- The official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` handles pagination, notifications, cancellation, lifecycle, output validation and attachment projection.
- Original `reverse-engineer-anything` skill, its upstream `tool_count` and all seven references. The plugin registers the package's skill with its own resource directory; it does not overwrite Codex/user skills.
- Original stateful upstream MCP process and complete Evidence `content`/`structuredContent`. No result summaries or reconstructed IDs.
- All **six original MCP prompts** with their 25 arguments and the original dynamic completions, reachable from the composer's `/` menu on the *same* REA Client, process and analysis session as the 229 tools.
dsh-rea README · What is preserved：REA is an exact npm dependency, not a reimplementation. Native engines and commercial licenses remain bring-your-own, exactly as upstream.

dsh-rea README · Prompt templates in the `/` menu：The six original prompts enter through the composer's own `/` menu, under the `rea` group (`/rea:investigate_feature`, `/rea:compare_application_versions`, `/rea:verify_reconstruction`, `/rea:trace_crash`, `/rea:audit_residual_unknowns`, `/rea:prepare_bounded_process_capture`) — the surface a Codex user already knows, where Codex exposes these same MCP prompts. **No extra button or permanent control is added to the composer.**

dsh-rea README · Prompt templates in the `/` menu：Picking an entry opens that template's argument form: the original argument descriptions, upstream argument completions (target documents, providers, procedures, retained Evidence, captures, manifests, occurrences, unresolved unknowns) and an exact-text preview you can insert into the draft.

Fidelity rules of that panel:

dsh-rea README · Prompt templates in the `/` menu：- Discovery and resolution are both originals: the menu lists `prompts/list`, the form calls `prompts/get`, and completions call `completion/complete` on the connection the tools already use — no second REA process, no rewritten templates, no cached or fabricated suggestions.
- A pick returns `handled`: the slash pipeline inserts and rewrites nothing, so choosing a template changes no draft text.
- Preview never executes analysis; every tool call stays a separate, explicit model decision.
- Insertion is a plain draft write. The panel never submits, never sends and never selects a target; you edit or send the draft yourself.
- A generation guard rejects a render whose answer arrives after the connection changed, so a stale template can never be inserted.
- The menu group is Web-only. CLI/headless profiles follow the same lazy rules; only the `/` group is absent.

dsh-rea README · Prompt templates in the `/` menu：Because DSH caches each package's client metadata for the lifetime of a Host process, adding this entry requires **one DSH restart** after upgrading: a running Host that already mounted `dsh-rea` before this version has cached it as a host-only package and will not serve the new bundle until it restarts. No configuration change is needed.

dsh-rea README · Install：This package is **not on npm** — the `dsh-rea` name on npm belongs to a different, unrelated adapter. Install it from the GitHub release tarball instead, which is what the plugin market's `github:` source consumes:

```text
https://github.com/JeremyWangCY/dsh-rea/releases/download/v0.5.0/dsh-rea-0.5.0.tgz
```

dsh-rea README · Install：A release asset is required (the market resolves the `releases/download/<tag>/<name>-<version>.tgz` URL): the repository alone is not enough because it is TypeScript-free only by accident — `lib/` ships pre-built, but there is no build step and no committed dist for other branches. Each release states the pinned `rea-agents` version in its notes.

dsh-rea README · Install：Verified before publishing: `pnpm test` 70/70, `pnpm verify` 35/35, `pnpm verify:lazy` 7/7, plus a live MCP handshake against the packed tarball (`initialize` → `tools/list` → 229 tools). `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` services are peer dependencies and are supplied by the DSH host, not by this package.

dsh-rea README · Install：For local development, install the absolute directory of this checkout through the plugin manager. Use the currently active profile; Web UI does not necessarily mean the `web` profile (desktop can host the same UI).

dsh-rea README · Configuration：The bundle inserts the host plugin. Defaults load the catalog on demand and leave DSH's native/PTC presentation untouched:

```yaml
- id: dsh-rea
  config:
    exposure: lazy
    serverName: rea

dsh-rea README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| enabled | true | Enable the plugin |
| exposure | lazy | `lazy` exposes the catalogue per agent and only after `/rea`; `always` restores the v0.3 always-on catalogue |
| keywordUnlock | false | Also let a real user message reveal the catalogue by mentioning reverse engineering. Off by default; see above |
| serverName | rea | Official bridge namespace |
| tools | all | Compatibility marker; subsets are no longer supported |
| nodeCommand | empty | Host executable; Electron uses `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`. Set an explicit supported Node if child analysis workers cannot use the host executable |
| env | {} | Explicit REA provider environment; official bridge scrubs inherited credential-shaped/DSH variables |
| toolCallTimeoutMs | 300000 | MCP call timeout; not an assurance that the outer agent/PTC deadline is longer |
| failOnStartupError | true | Report startup failure rather than silently exposing an empty tool set |

dsh-rea README · Configuration：Supported Node range: `^22.19.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0`; 23/25 are unsupported. No runtime or analysis engine is installed/upgraded by plugin activation. Existing unrelated approval/preset settings are not changed. Automatic reconnection is disabled deliberately: a new REA process loses target/provider/retained Evidence state; reload explicitly after a disconnect.

dsh-rea README · Native versus PTC：All tools remain registered in both modes. PTC belongs to DSH's tools/agent preset, not REA; the plugin does not switch every other tool into PTC.

Measured in an isolated real Cordis deployment on this machine:

| Presentation | Model-side tool JSON | Generated SDK text |
|---|---:|---:|
| native, all 229 | 273,264 bytes | 0 |
| PTC, `run_code` only | 944 bytes | 172,198 bytes |

dsh-rea README · Native versus PTC：These are **bytes, not tokenizer counts**. The previous v0.1 claim of ~543k input tokens incorrectly counted MCP output schemas as model input. PTC is not zero-context; SDK text is in the prompt. Its default worker wall limit is 600s, compute limit 60s and output limit 64MiB. Only returned/printed values become the outer result, so return complete Evidence when needed. PTC and native preserve tool results, but they are different model interfaces and are not proven to produce identical answers.

dsh-rea README · Native versus PTC：Use the original skill's routing, Evidence and provider-recovery instructions. REA CLI JSON also preserves full Evidence IDs; unlike long-lived MCP it is normally one-shot and does not retain a provider/target across commands. CLI output still consumes context if fed back to the model.

dsh-rea README · Verification and limits：`verify/integration.mjs` runs the real Cordis ToolRuntime, original upstream MCP and DSH worker-thread PTC, then deeply compares results. Covered: every upstream name/description/input schema, original skill, the six original prompt metadata sets and their rendered messages, an original provider completion, JS analysis and data-flow tracing, retained-reference view, Evidence bundle listing, a one-record offline HAR, one-member ZIP lifecycle/inventory, upstream errors, pre-dispatch cancellation, disposal, explicit startup failure. `test/client.test.mjs` loads the real browser bundle against a minimal React/DOM harness and drives the actual `/` source: idle silence (the session slot renders nothing and no request is sent), source registration, candidate filtering, a `handled` pick that writes no draft, argument gating, completion payloads, exact preview text, draft-preserving insertion through `setDraft` only, error surfacing, and the post-upgrade restart hint. `verify/connection.mjs` mounts the real installed `WebServer` + `Connection` and speaks the real wire: 401 without the browser session, then `prompts/list`/`get`/`complete` deep-equal t

dsh-rea README · Verification and limits：Not claimed: all upstream operations executed; native decompilers/ADB/JEB/browser capture equivalence; mid-flight expensive-operation cancellation; identical LLM answers; every model provider's schema limits; exhaustive completion coverage for every external provider. External providers require task-specific verification.

dsh-rea README · Verification and limits：The official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` exposes no shared-connection hook, so `lib/vendor/mcp-bridge.js` is a verbatim MIT copy of that bridge (upstream SHA-256 recorded in its header) with exactly one reviewed local change: an optional fourth `onClient` argument. Tool registration, transport, reconnect, error and disposal behavior are byte-identical to upstream, and `test/plugin.test.mjs` re-derives and compares the whole file so it cannot silently drift. The official bridge also does not copy MCP annotations to ToolRuntime metadata; required-task execution would be unsupported. See [the bounded verification report](verification/README.md) for environment, methods and exact limitations.

dsh-rea README · Migration from v0.1：Remove old `tools: entry/navigate/analyze`, `runner` and `version` overrides. Version comes from the exact dependency; all tools are restored, public prefix changes from `rea__` to `mcp__rea__`. New naming matches DSH's official bridge.

dsh-rea README · Upgrading the pinned REA release：The dependency is an exact pin, so a new REA release is adopted by changing that one
line and re-verifying — no adapter source change is expected, because the plugin reads
the version and the catalog size from the installed package instead of carrying literals:

```sh
pnpm add rea-agents@<new-version>
node verify/measure.mjs     # regenerates verification/schema-measurement.json
pnpm test && pnpm verify && pnpm verify:lazy
```

dsh-rea README · Upgrading the pinned REA release：Then update the version, tool count, prompt-argument count and byte figures in
`README.md`, `README.zh.md` and `verification/README.md`. `pnpm verify` derives the
count itself, so a catalog change surfaces as a failure in the deep comparison rather
than as a silently stale document.
dsh-rea README · License：This adapter is MIT. REA is by morluto and contributors, MIT, included as a pinned dependency with its upstream license. Third-party tools retain their own licenses.
